title: Beyond Sample Hardness: Adaptive Data Selection through Learning Dynamics
abstract: arXiv:2611.27656v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Data selection has emerged as an effective approach to reducing the model training costs. However, most existing methods often rely heavily on sample hardness, which may overlook differences in sample learning dynamics and lead to suboptimal sample selection. In this paper, we propose LeDAS, an end-to-end Learning Dynamics-Aware Selection framework for dynamic data selection, which jointly characterizes sample importance through hardness, learning progress, and deterioration, enabling adaptive sample prioritization throughout training with marginal additional computational overhead. Specifically, we track per-sample loss dynamics using exponential moving averages (EMA) to obtain three complementary signals that capture current learning difficulty, ongoing learning improvements, and potential degradation. translated_title: 超越样本难度：基于学习动态的自适应数据选择
translated_abstract: 数据选择已成为降低模型训练成本的有效方法。然而，大多数现有方法往往严重依赖样本难度，这可能忽视样本学习动态之间的差异，从而导致次优的样本选择。在本文中，我们提出了LeDAS，一个端到端的学习动态感知选择框架，用于动态数据选择。该框架通过难度、学习进展和退化三个方面共同刻画样本重要性，能够以极小的额外计算开销在整个训练过程中实现自适应的样本优先级排序。具体而言，我们使用指数移动平均（EMA）追踪每个样本的损失动态，获得三个互补信号，分别捕捉当前的学习难度、正在发生的学习改进以及潜在的退化。为了适应不断演变的训练动态，我们引入了自适应度量融合，这是一种基于上下文老虎机的机制，能够动态调整……
tldr: 该论文提出LeDAS框架，通过难度、学习进展和退化三个学习动态信号自适应地选择训练数据，并利用基于上下文老虎机的自适应度量融合机制动态调整样本优先级，以极小的额外计算开销克服了传统仅依赖样本难度的数据选择方法的局限性。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes LeDAS, an end-to-end learning dynamics-aware data selection framework that adaptively prioritizes samples by jointly characterizing hardness, learning progress, and deterioration, with a contextual bandit-based adaptive metric fusion mechanism, achieving better selection at marginal computational overhead.
